name: narrative-graph
description: narrative-graph reads narrative prose and returns candidate relational facts: who is related to whom, how, with what confidence, and where in the text the claim was made. It detects entities, labels relations with a rule-based English pattern pack, aggregates restatements of the same fact across a whole document, and flags contradictions between them. Everything runs locally and deterministically with no language model and no network call. It ships as a Rust crate and a Node.js package with generated TypeScript types, and its output is shaped to feed a knowledge store such as holographic-memory.
description_good_justification: README.md opens with a one-sentence description of what the software does and who it is for: "Turn prose into candidate relational facts, entirely local. No LLM, no network. Entities, relations, confidence scores and spans, for Rust and Node.". The same description is in Cargo.toml and package.json.
interact_justification: README.md has Install (crates.io and npm), API, and Contributing sections; CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to set up a development environment and open a pull request; feedback goes through GitHub Issues at https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-graph/issues.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md describes the process: clone, build, run the Rust and Node test suites, then open a pull request against main; pull requests are reviewed through GitHub.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the acceptance requirements: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo test --all-features`, `npm test`, and `npm run test:types` must pass; new extraction rules need a test with a realistic sentence and a stated expected candidate; commit messages use `<type>: <description>`.
floss_license_justification: Apache License 2.0, declared as license = "Apache-2.0" in Cargo.toml and package.json, with the full text in LICENSE.
license_location_justification: The complete Apache-2.0 text is in LICENSE at the repository root, and GitHub's license detection identifies it as Apache-2.0.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md covers installation, what the software analyzes, the API, requirements, and development; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md explains the design and docs/INTEGRATION.md shows how to use the library from other tools; docs/EVALUATION.md records measured precision and recall on public-domain novels.
documentation_interface_justification: The Node interface is fully typed in index.d.ts, generated from the Rust types with ts-rs; every public Rust item carries a doc comment and the crate builds with rustdoc (documentation = https://docs.rs/narrative-graph).
sites_https_justification: The project site and repository are https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-graph (HTTPS). The package pages https://www.npmjs.com/package/narrative-graph and https://crates.io/crates/narrative-graph are HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues at https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-graph/issues is the discussion mechanism: searchable, URL-addressable, usable from any browser with a free GitHub account, no proprietary client required.
english_justification: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, docs/*.md, code comments, and commit messages are written in English.
maintained_justification: The repository has had commits within the last month (October 2026), Dependabot pull requests are reviewed and merged as they arrive, and bug reports are answered by the maintainer.
repo_track_justification: Git records author, date, and diff for every change; git log shows named authors for every commit.
repo_interim_justification: Interim commits are pushed to main continuously between releases (dozens of commits between v0.1.1 and v0.1.2, and more since).
repo_distributed_justification: Git is a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml and package.json both declare version 0.1.2; each release is a unique semantic version with matching git tags v0.1.1 and v0.1.2.
version_semver_justification: Versions follow Semantic Versioning (0.1.2 today) as recorded in Cargo.toml, package.json, and CHANGELOG.md, which states adherence to SemVer.
version_tags_justification: Each release is tagged in git as v<version> (v0.1.1, v0.1.2), and the tags match the GitHub Releases.
release_notes_justification: Every GitHub Release carries human-written notes (v0.1.2 describes the three new relation forms and the measured recall change over a 1.96 MB corpus). CHANGELOG.md keeps the same notes in Keep a Changelog format with Added/Changed/Fixed sections.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed in any release, so there are none to list.
report_process_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and the README Contributing section direct bug reports to the GitHub issue tracker at https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-graph/issues, and SECURITY.md covers security reports separately.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues at https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-graph/issues tracks each report individually with number, state, and labels.
report_responses_justification: All bug reports to date (issues #1 through #9) received a response and were resolved; the issues are maintainer-filed and closed with the fixing commit linked, so there is no unanswered external report. The first external report will be answered the same way.
enhancement_responses_justification: Every enhancement request filed so far (issues #1 through #9, covering aggregation, coreference, contradiction detection, temporal validity, correction feedback, and language packs) was answered and implemented, with the closing commit linked from the issue.
report_archive_justification: All issues and pull requests, with their responses, are publicly archived and searchable at https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-graph/issues?q=is%3Aissue.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md (repository root) tells reporters to use GitHub private vulnerability reporting at https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-graph/security/advisories/new or email admin@writerslogic.com, and asks for reproduction steps and impact.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md gives two private channels: GitHub private security advisories and admin@writerslogic.com.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received yet, so there is nothing to measure against the 14-day target; SECURITY.md commits to an initial response within a few days.
build_justification: The Rust library builds with `cargo build`; the Node addon builds with `npm run build` (napi-rs); both are documented in README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md and run in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml).
build_common_tools_justification: Cargo and npm, the standard tools for Rust and Node, are the only build tools.
build_floss_tools_justification: Cargo, rustc, Node, npm, and @napi-rs/cli are all FLOSS.
test_justification: Automated test suite: 99 Rust unit and integration tests (src/ and tests/heuristic.rs) run with `cargo test`; Node binding tests in tests/node run with `npm test` (node --test) plus a strict TypeScript check of the generated bindings (`npm run test:types`).
test_invocation_justification: `cargo test` and `npm test` run the whole suite with no manual steps; CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md document both.
test_most_justification: 99 Rust tests cover segmentation, entity detection, every relation pattern, aggregation, and conflict detection; 13 Node tests cover the full binding surface; docs/EVALUATION.md adds a measured precision/recall harness over public-domain novels.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs fmt, clippy, the Rust tests, the Node build and tests, and the TypeScript check on every push to main and every pull request.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires that new functionality comes with tests: new analyzers must include a test against a realistic passage whose expected result was authored independently of the implementation.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent feature commits add tests alongside the code (for example the pronoun-carry change af1c91d shipped with the test commit e0f4e6c, and each relation form added in v0.1.2 has its own test).
tests_documented_added_justification: The test requirement is stated in CONTRIBUTING.md under "Before opening a PR".
warnings_justification: CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`; rustc warnings are denied through the same clippy invocation.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any warning, so main carries zero rustc or clippy warnings.
warnings_strict_justification: `-D warnings` turns every rustc and clippy warning into an error in CI, and clippy runs with --all-targets.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design principles: the library is a pure function from text to a result, with no network, no filesystem access beyond an explicitly supplied model path, no shared mutable state, and input bounds enforced on sizes (see SECURITY.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer is familiar with common error classes (injection, memory safety, integer overflow, denial of service through unbounded input). Rust's type system and the absence of unsafe code address memory safety; inputs are bounded.
crypto_published_justification: The project implements no cryptographic functionality.
crypto_call_justification: The project implements no cryptographic functionality.
crypto_floss_justification: The project implements no cryptographic functionality.
crypto_keylength_justification: The project implements no cryptographic functionality.
crypto_working_justification: The project implements no cryptographic functionality.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The project implements no cryptographic functionality.
crypto_pfs_justification: The project implements no network protocols.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The project stores no passwords or credentials.
crypto_random_justification: The project generates no security-relevant random values.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases are delivered through the npm registry and crates.io over HTTPS with registry-side integrity hashes; source is delivered from GitHub over HTTPS.
delivery_unsigned_justification: npm packages are published with npm provenance (Sigstore attestations linking the package to the GitHub Actions run), which npm verifies on install, so a man-in-the-middle cannot substitute an unsigned package.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No open medium-or-higher vulnerability is known. Dependabot alerts, Dependabot updates, and cargo-deny advisory checks (deny.toml) are enabled so any new one is surfaced promptly.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No unpatched critical vulnerability has been reported.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository contains no credentials; publishing tokens live in GitHub Actions secrets and CI uses OIDC provenance.
static_analysis_justification: Two static analysers run in CI on every pull request: clippy with -D warnings (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and CodeQL for Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, and GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/codeql.yml). OpenSSF Scorecard runs weekly (.github/workflows/scorecard.yml).
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security query suite looks for common vulnerabilities in the Rust and JavaScript code on every pull request and on a weekly schedule.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: There are no open CodeQL or clippy findings; CI fails on any clippy finding, and CodeQL results are reviewed in the repository's code scanning tab.
static_analysis_often_justification: clippy and CodeQL run on every pull request and every push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: A cargo-fuzz target (fuzz/fuzz_targets/extract_triples.rs) drives the public extractors with arbitrary bounded input; fuzz/README.md documents how to run it.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz target is built with debug assertions and overflow checks on (cargo-fuzz's default dev profile), so Rust's integer-overflow and bounds checks act as assertions during fuzzing.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The project is written in Rust with zero `unsafe` blocks (grep -rn unsafe src returns nothing), so it is not written in a memory-unsafe language.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis has reported a vulnerability.
